articles.title: In 1985, she started a paper business with with 3,800 US dollars; 21 years later, she became China’s richest person: How Zhang Yin turned America’s waste paper into a paper empire
articles.summary: In 1985, business tycoon Zhang Yin started a paper-trading business in Hong Kong with about 30,000 yuan, or 3,800 US dollars.
articles.body: In 1985, business tycoon Zhang Yin started a paper-trading business in Hong Kong with about 30,000 yuan, or 3,800 US dollars. More than two decades later, she would be named China's richest person, with an estimated fortune of $3.4 billion on the 2006 Hurun Rich List. The material at the centre of her business was something most people had already thrown away: waste paper. Zhang eventually built a business that collected recovered paper in the United States, shipped it to China and used it as raw material for paper and packaging products.She saw value in something others discardedAccording to a 2007 profile in The New York Times, Zhang entered the paper trade when China was facing a shortage of paper-making raw material and its manufacturing industry was beginning to expand. In Hong Kong, she learned about the waste-paper business. Zhang recalled advice she had received from a man in the industry. “Wastepaper is like a forest. Paper recycles itself, generation after generation,” she told the NY Times.She later arrived in Hong Kong from Guangdong in 1985 and started her own company with 30,000 yuan after turning down a job offer. She began buying scrap paper through intermediaries in the United States. The business soon showed her that Hong Kong alone would not be enough. China's growing manufacturing sector needed cardboard and packaging, while the United States had a much larger supply of used paper. So Zhang looked towards America.In 1990, she moved to Los AngelesAs reported by The LA Times, Zhang began collecting waste paper in Los Angeles in 1990 and shipping it to China, where it was used to make cardboard needed by the country's growing export industries. Her company, America Chung Nam, was already on track to ship about 3 million tons of waste paper in 2002, almost all of it to China. The operation was initially small.Zhang and her husband had driven around the United States in a used Dodge minivan, approaching garbage dumps for scrap paper. The couple had formed their US recycling company in the 1990s to collect paper and ship it to China. Zhang later described how difficult those early years were. Speaking to reporters in Hong Kong in November 2006, she said: “I had to learn from scratch. The business was just my husband and me, and I didn’t speak a word of English.” “It was my hard work that helped me achieve my success,” she added.The shipping problem had an unusual solutionThere was one major difficulty with Zhang's business: waste paper was bulky and had to travel from the US to China. But the existing trade between the two countries offered an opportunity. Chinese ships were carrying manufactured goods to the United States. Some vessels had considerable unused space on their return journey. According to The Economic Times, Rupert Hoogewerf, publisher of the Hurun Report, said Zhang secured low shipping rates because many vessels were almost empty after unloading their cargo in the US. That helped make the long-distance movement of waste paper commercially viable.The basic chain was straightforward: recovered paper collected in America went to China, where paper manufacturers could process it into new packaging material. Chinese container ships commonly unloaded goods in US ports and returned to China carrying American waste paper.'America Chung Nam' became a major exporterThe company Zhang built in the United States was ‘America Chung Nam.’ The company was the biggest waste-paper exporter in the US at the time. It reported that America Chung Nam had sales of $238 million in 2001 and that its export volume had put it at the top of the Journal of Commerce's list of the nation's biggest exporters. The company maintained that position for 18 consecutive years. By then, Zhang had identified a much larger opportunity. She did not want to remain only the company collecting and exporting the raw material. She wanted to manufacture the paper herself.She moved from recycling into manufacturingIn 1995, Dongguan Nine Dragons was established to manufacture containerboard in Dongguan, Guangdong, according to Nine Dragons' own listing documents filed with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The company's first paper machine began production in July 1998. Its design capacity was 200,000 tonnes a year. The expansion was rapid. Nine Dragons' listing document says a second paper machine, with a design capacity of 400,000 tonnes a year, began production in June 2000. The company's manufacturing capacity subsequently rose to 3.3 million tonnes a year by the time of its 2006 listing documents. This is the point at which Zhang's business moved beyond simply collecting America's discarded paper. Her companies were now involved in both sides of the process: sourcing recovered paper and manufacturing packaging paper in China.China's export boom created a huge market for cardboardChina's manufacturing and export industries were expanding rapidly, creating demand for cardboard and containerboard used to package goods. Chinese companies making products ranging from computers to bicycles were demanding more cardboard boxes, while China's paper industry was expanding to meet that demand. A Forest Trends report published in 2007 also found that waste paper accounted for about 60% of the fibre used to manufacture paper and paperboard products in China at the time. It said about three-quarters of China's waste-paper fibre was used to manufacture corrugated cardboard boxes for Chinese goods shipped to overseas markets. That gave Zhang's business a direct connection to China's export economy. American waste paper could become Chinese packaging, and that packaging could then be used for goods being exported around the world.The next major turning point came in 2006Nine Dragons Paper was listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on March 3, 2006, according to the company's annual report. Seven months later, Zhang appeared at the top of China's Hurun Rich List. Hurun's own 2006 report said that 49-year-old Zhang Yin had wealth of 27 billion yuan, making her China's first female richest person. It also said Nine Dragons had a market value of 37.5 billion yuan and that Zhang owned 72% of the company. An AFP report put her fortune at approximately $3.4 billion. She had risen from 36th place the previous year to No. 1, according to the report. It also described her as the first woman to top China's annual rich list.Speaking to reporters in Hong Kong in November 2006, she described how she viewed it differently from most people: “Other people saw scrap paper as garbage, but I saw it as a forest of trees.” She also told reporters, “Chinese manufacturers were desperate for scrap paper.” “All I did was help fulfill a need,” she added.Where is Zhang Yin now?According to Nine Dragons Paper’s current corporate information, she is still the company’s Chairlady, a position she has held since 2006. According to Forbers, her current net worth is around $1.7B (on Sep 23). Zhang's husband Liu Ming Chung, the CEO of Nine Dragons, is also a billionaire.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 1 Indian killed, 19 rescued after MV Cape Dao attacked off Oman; MEA calls for end to shipping attacks
articles.summary: An Indian seafarer, identified as Wiper Suraj Yadav from Uttar Pradesh, was killed after a missile attack on the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier
articles.body: An Indian seafarer, identified as Wiper Suraj Yadav from Uttar Pradesh, was killed after a missile attack on the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier MV Cape Dao off the east coast of Oman, while all 19 other Indian crew members were safely evacuated, the government said on Wednesday.Yadav succumbed to head injuries sustained in the attack, Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said. The vessel had 20 Indian seafarers on board, with the surviving crew evacuated by the Royal Navy of Oman and brought ashore.Sonowal said directions had been issued to maritime authorities to coordinate with Omani authorities and the ship management company for the immediate and safe repatriation of the surviving Indian crew.“The government will ensure that the mortal remains of Suraj Yadav are brought home with full dignity, and every possible support is extended to his next of kin,” Sonowal said.India condemns attackThe ministry of external affairs condemned the attack and said continuing incidents targeting commercial shipping in the region were “deeply worrisome”.“Of the 20 Indian seafarers on board, 19 have been rescued, while 1 Indian national tragically lost his life. We offer our deepest condolences to the family of the deceased,” the MEA said.The ministry said its embassy in Oman was closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with Omani authorities for the early repatriation of the Indian seafarers. It also thanked the Omani authorities for their support.“We condemn the attack on the commercial vessel MV Cape Dao earlier today off the east coast of Oman,” the MEA said.It called for an end to attacks targeting commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region. India also reiterated its call for free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways.“The continuing incidents of attacks on commercial shipping in the region are deeply worrisome. We reiterate our call for dialogue and diplomacy to de-escalate tensions and enable early return of peace to the region,” the MEA said.Embassy coordinating with OmanThe Indian embassy in Oman said it was in close coordination with Omani authorities over the safety of the crew and was monitoring the situation.“We are closely monitoring the attack on MV Cape Dao today while transiting toward India, and are in close coordination with Omani authorities regarding the safety of all crew on board, including 19 Indian nationals,” the embassy said in a post on X.The mission also expressed condolences to the family of the Indian seafarer who was killed.“We are deeply saddened by the loss of one Indian national in this attack. Our heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family. The Mission is coordinating with the RPSL and is in touch with the family of the deceased,” it added.The MEA said the embassy was proactively coordinating with the Omani authorities for the early repatriation of the Indian seafarers. Government orders repatriationSonowal said maritime authorities had been directed to work closely with Omani authorities and the ship management company to ensure the surviving crew members return home safely.He also offered condolences to Yadav’s family and said the government would provide all possible support to his next of kin.India has consistently called for safe and free navigation in international waters and the unhindered flow of commerce through international waterways.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: JANDIALA GURU: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal on Wednesday accused the Bhagwant Mann government of allegedly repackaging welfare
articles.body: JANDIALA GURU: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal on Wednesday accused the Bhagwant Mann government of allegedly repackaging welfare schemes launched by the previous SAD government and taking credit for them, while allowing law and order and governance to deteriorate.Addressing a gathering during the SAD’s Punjab Bachao campaign, Badal said the government’s “Mann De Manaufe” report merely showcased schemes such as Atta-Dal, Shagun, old-age pension and Teerath Yatra, which, he claimed, were started during Parkash Singh Badal’s tenure.He alleged that several schemes had subsequently been diluted or discontinued. Under Atta-Dal, the earlier 30-kg wheat entitlement had been reduced to 5 kg, he claimed, while free bicycles for girl students, village sports kits, free chemist shops, gyms, RO plants and Suvidha and Sanjh Kendras had also been discontinued.Turning to law and order, Badal alleged that Punjab had witnessed a serious deterioration under the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government, pointing to the killing of two ASIs and bomb blasts at police stations.He also levelled allegations of corruption in postings and transfers and made a serious allegation involving the chief minister’s wife, referring to an alleged demand for a Rs 5-crore bribe.Badal also accused Akali Dal Waris Punjab De of functioning as the “B team” of AAP and alleged that the organisation was receiving financial support from the ruling dispensation.He further alleged that the drug menace had multiplied under the AAP government because of alleged political patronage to traffickers.On the SAD’s proposed agenda, Badal promised skill universities in every district, one-month tubewell connections for farmers without them, 50 kg wheat under Atta-Dal, a Rs 1 lakh Shagun benefit, Rs 3,100 monthly old-age pension, loans of up to Rs 10 lakh for youth entrepreneurs and 75% subsidy for milch animals.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Amritsar | Silver Rate in Amritsar | Bank Holidays in Amritsar | Public Holidays in Amritsar | Petrol Price in Amritsar | Diesel Price in Amritsar | CNG Price in Amritsar | LPG Price in AmritsarStay updated with the latest Amritsar news. articles.title: Astha Kunj gang rape: Trio trailed teens for a kilometre, coordinated assault over phone
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The three men accused of gangraping a 17-year-old girl at Astha Kunj Park in southeast Delhi followed her for nearly a kilometer before closing
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The three men accused of gangraping a 17-year-old girl at Astha Kunj Park in southeast Delhi followed her for nearly a kilometer before closing in, after which they took turns sexually assaulting her at different locations including benches, summoning each other to the spots over phone calls, police said on Wednesday, according to PTI.With investigation into the case deepening, it has also emerged that one of the accused, Hemant, an advocate aged around 24, was removed from a gym about a month ago after its management allegedly received several complaints from women regarding his behaviour, a senior police officer said.Accused trio 'frequented' the parkThe probe has also revealed that the three accused — Asif, a vegetable wholesaler aged around 32, Hemant, and his brother Mahesh, a final-year BSc Mathematics student aged around 24 — used to frequent the park and allegedly lurk in its secluded areas, police said. Police also said Hemant and Mahesh showed "no remorse" during their initial questioning, according to officials.The investigation has also raised suspicion that the accused may have been involved in similar incidents at the park earlier. Police are checking their criminal records and past activities to ascertain whether such allegations can be substantiated. According to police sources, no formal complaint in this regard had been received. Investigators suspect that some victims may have refrained from approaching police due to fear of social stigma.Birthday visit to Kalkaji temple turned into nightmareInvestigators said the present incident occurred between 7.15pm and 8pm on Monday. The girl and her 17-year-old friend went to Astha Kunj Park after offering prayers at Kalkaji Mandir on the occasion of her 17th birthday, and entered the grounds through Gate No. 7, when the accused trio spotted them."They followed them for nearly a kilometer and then confronted them. They threatened the duo by posing as police personnel and warned them of registering a case against them," another senior officer said, PTI reported.Accused 'threatened duo before separating the girlThe accused then allegedly separated the girl from her friend. Asif — who is married and has a 13-year-old daughter — allegedly threatened them with a knife and a firearm, before the trio left with the girl, allegedly taking her to multiple secluded locations inside the park where she was sexually assaulted.Police said while one accused allegedly assaulted the girl, another kept watch, and repeatedly called each other over mobile phones after one had finished, summoning the other to the spot. Asif, a resident of Tughlakabad who works at the Sriniwaspuri mandi, has known Hemant and Mahesh for around four years, police said.'No security guard was found at the spot'After the alleged assault, the three fled. The girl and her friend managed to leave the park and called the PCR from the boy's phone. They were standing near Gate No. 7 when a police team reached them. A senior officer said no security guard could be located at the spot at that time. Police are now examining the deployment of guards at the park as well as security arrangements there.The investigation has also highlighted inadequate lighting and absence of CCTV cameras at the location where the alleged sexual assault took place. However, police arrested all three accused, including one who was injured in retaliatory firing after allegedly opening fire at a police team early Tuesday, officials said.The girl's account significantly helped investigators as she was able to recall the physical descriptions of the men, their nicknames, complexion and clothes they were wearing. She also told police that the men did not appear to be vagabonds or otherwise suspicious, according to the officer.Police subsequently scanned footage from more than 300 CCTV cameras in and around the park and on routes leading to and from the area. Investigators shortlisted around 20 persons before technical surveillance and local intelligence helped them zero in on the three accused, who are locals and allegedly frequent visitors to the park.All 3 sent to judicial custodyPolice are now examining the accused's mobile phones, contacts and technical evidence to reconstruct their movements and establish their interactions before and after the incident. All three accused have been sent to judicial custody. Police are likely to seek their custody after certain aspects of the technical investigation are complete, officials said.Investigators are also checking whether the accused have been previously involved in any such incidents, and whether complaints against Hemant at the gym have any connection with the present case.(With agency inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assaul)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Why Iran looms large over Trump-Xi talks in White House
articles.summary: Iran could emerge as a sensitive issue when US President Donald Trump meets Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington on Thursday, amid a report that
articles.body: Iran could emerge as a sensitive issue when US President Donald Trump meets Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington on Thursday, amid a report that Chinese entities provided Tehran with high-resolution satellite imagery before an Iranian missile strike that killed three US troops in Jordan.Trump is expected to "confront" Xi over Beijing's alleged support for Iran when the two leaders meet, after a report linked Chinese entities to satellite imagery provided to Tehran before the deadly Iranian strike on US troops, reported Fox News.Satellite imagery linked to Iran strikeThe reported imagery was allegedly obtained by Iran before its July 17 missile attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, where three US troops were killed and four others wounded. US officials have linked the imagery to the attack, according to The Wall Street Journal, describing it as the clearest evidence so far that Chinese support for Iran had lethal consequences for US forces.The US officials did not identify the Chinese entities involved and did not accuse Beijing of directly participating in the attack. China has also rejected US concerns over Chinese companies providing satellite imagery to Iran.Trump on Sunday had also acknowledged the broader intelligence rivalry between Washington and Beijing when asked about the report. "You know what they say? That China spies on us. I say you're right, and we spy on them, too," Trump said.Asked whether he planned to raise the issue with Xi, Trump said the Chinese president had "behaved reasonably well" and that "we behave reasonably well."The latest report comes after months of US warnings to Beijing over Chinese companies allegedly providing satellite imagery that Iran could use to target US forces. In May, the Trump administration sanctioned three Chinese companies, accusing them of providing, collecting or publishing imagery that could help Iran target American personnel.US officials had also raised the issue with their Chinese counterparts before the latest report emerged. Beijing has denied that Chinese companies were involved in supplying imagery for attacks on US forces.The July 17 strike marked a major escalation in attacks on US forces. Iranian ballistic missiles struck a housing area at the Jordanian base where American troops were staying, killing three soldiers and wounding four others. Iran also targeted aircraft at the base, according to US officials.The reported Chinese imagery is part of broader US concerns about Chinese technology and data being used by Iran, including satellite imagery, navigation services and components for drones and missiles. US officials and analysts say such assistance could improve Iran's ability to identify and strike American military targets.The issue had also come up in US-China diplomatic exchanges. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi days after the July 17 attack. Asked whether China was providing Iran with targeting information, Rubio declined to answer directly, saying "nothing that China has done has in any way changed the trajectory of the conflict."Also read: China warns Trump not to cross 4 ‘red lines’ as Xi heads to USTrade, AI and Taiwan also on tableXi's visit to Washington from September 23 to 25 is expected to cover a wide range of issues beyond Iran, with trade, artificial intelligence, rare earths and Taiwan among the key areas of discussion. The two sides are also seeking to maintain stability in their economic relationship, with the existing trade truce set to expire in November.Trump is expected to personally greet Xi at Joint Base Andrews when the Chinese president arrives in the Washington area, before the two leaders hold formal talks at the White House on Thursday.The summit comes as Washington and Beijing seek to manage tensions over tariffs, technology restrictions and Taiwan, while also competing over artificial intelligence and critical minerals.The reported satellite support could therefore add another point of tension to the Trump-Xi meeting, even as both sides seek to keep their broader relationship stable and prevent disputes from escalating.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'International system broken': Rubio's stark message amid UNGA, says US interests above world order
articles.summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Wednesday said the world lacks a functional international system capable of addressing major conflicts.
articles.body: US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Wednesday said the world lacks a functional international system capable of addressing major conflicts. He listed out the nations at dispute, as he argued that countries will act in their own national interests when global mechanisms fail.Speaking to reporters during the UN general assembly week in New York, Rubio said there was broad agreement among world leaders that the international system was failing. He said the system had moved beyond its intended role and was unable to resolve major conflicts.“It would be great if we had a functional international system, for example, that could deal with a war between Thailand and Cambodia that occurred...Right now, we don't seem to have a functional international system that can address it,” Rubio said.‘International system is failing’Rubio said multiple leaders had raised concerns about the functioning of the international system during the high-level UNGA week.“I think multiple leaders...pointed to the fact that the international system is failing, and it's failing because it has grown beyond its mandate. It has grown beyond its intent. It's involved in all kinds of things that it shouldn't be involved in, and it's unable to solve virtually any major conflict in the world,” he said.The US secretary of state said there was “unanimity and consensus” among leaders that the system was broken.“But it's broken because it broke itself. It needs to be brought back to its proper focus and its proper role,” Rubio said.US sees ‘utility’ in international systemDespite his criticism, Rubio said Washington recognised the value of the international system and remained engaged with it.“We see the utility in the international system. We're here...I think the President has said that the United Nations, for example, has tremendous potential, but it's not living up to it...,” he told reporters.Rubio also said that when international mechanisms fail to address conflicts, individual countries will prioritise their own interests.The remarks also come as US President Donald Trump addressed the UN general assembly on Tuesday and claimed that his administration had helped resolve several international disputes.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pakistan appoints former army general Nauman Mahmood as first head of Mecca alliance
articles.summary: Pakistan on Wednesday appointed a former Pakistan Army officer as the first secretary-general of the country's trilateral Mecca pact with Türkiye and
articles.body: Pakistan on Wednesday appointed a former Pakistan Army officer as the first secretary-general of the country's trilateral Mecca pact with Türkiye and Saudi Arabia.Lieutenant general Nauman Mahmood (retired) will head the alliance’s general secretariat, which is being established in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.“The government of Pakistan is pleased to announce the appointment of Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood, Hilal-i-Imtiaz (Military), (retired), as the first secretary general pursuant to the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement,” Pakistan’s Foreign Office said in a statement.Mahmood, who served in the military’s Baloch Regiment, previously commanded a key Pakistan Army corps in the country’s restive northwest and also served as president of the National Defence University in Islamabad.His appointment comes amid an escalation involving Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, the Yemeni rebels who have carried out attacks on Saudi territory in recent days and established control over the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait in the Red Sea.Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Türkiye signed the Mecca pact on August 7.Modelled on Nato’s Article 5, the agreement establishes a framework for collective deterrence and stipulates that an armed attack against any one member would be regarded as an attack against all three.The alliance held its inaugural meeting on August 31 in Istanbul, Türkiye, where officials from the three member states met to establish its institutional structure. They decided that the first secretary-general would be from Pakistan, paving the way for Mahmood’s appointment.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Singapore Airlines passenger died of cardiac arrest after turbulence, inquest told
articles.summary: Geoff Kitchen died onboard a Singapore Airlines flight which experienced severe turbulence in 2024.
articles.body:
A British man who died on board a Singapore Airlines flight, suffered a cardiac arrest after the plane was hit by severe turbulence, an inquest has been told.

Geoff Kitchen, from Thornbury in South Gloucestershire, died on 21 May 2024 after the Boeing 777 plane travelling from London Heathrow to Singapore encountered a sudden drop in altitude near the south western region of Myanmar.

The plane was later diverted to Bangkok, Thailand, where the 73-year-old was pronounced dead.

Dr Peter Harrowing, assistant coroner for Avon, said: "I am satisfied that it was the physiological effect of the aircraft turbulence which precipitated the cardiac arrest and ultimately Geoff's demise."

Harrowing reached the narrative conclusion into Kitchen's death at a hearing at Avon Coroners' Court earlier.

He told the inquest Kitchen, who had a history of coronary artery disease, had also been "thrown from his seat and landed on an adjacent passenger" during the incident.

Kitchen, a retired insurance professional, had flown out of Heathrow for a six-week holiday to Singapore, Indonesia and Australia with his wife, Linda.

In a statement read to the inquest, Linda said her husband had been listening to a podcast before the plane experienced a "huge drop or lunge".

She said she had began "screaming" and felt "incredible pain" as Kitchen had pressed her to the side, which caused injury to her back.

She also suffered a head wound which was "bleeding profusely".

Kitchen was later moved to the front of the plane to be given CPR, but Linda, who sustained spinal fractures, said nobody told her he had died until two days later.

Linda spent 10 days in hospital before she was airlifted back to Bristol, where she spent another week in hospital.

An initial post-mortem examination held in Thailand found Kitchen had died from congestive heart failure.

The inquest earlier was told he had undergone an operation to fit stents to his right coronary artery in April 2019.

However, a review in October that year found he had returned to "normal exercise capacity", a statement from his GP said.

Dr Edward Sheffield, who performed an additional post mortem on Kitchen's body in Bristol, said his cause of death was cardiac failure due to coronary artery atheroma and the physiological effects of turbulence.

A report into the incident, which Harrowing partially read to the inquest, said 56 people had been seriously injured, 23 suffered minor injuries and one man - Kitchen - had died.

"The aircraft was cruising at 37,000ft (11277.6m) when it was approaching the west coast of south-western Myanmar.

"At 07:49 GMT, the aircraft flew past a waypoint when the aircraft experienced severe turbulence.

"By 07:53, the aircraft had stabilised," the report said.

The crew reported the severe turbulence and made a Mayday call at 08:01 with a request to divert to Bangkok.

The plane landed there at 08:45, where it was met by medical personnel.

Linda launched legal action at the High Court against Singapore Airlines last month , seeking damages to help her access specialist support for her back.

The head of Singapore Airlines, Goh Choon Phong, previously apologised for the "traumatic experience" for those onboard flight SQ321.

He had also expressed his condolences to Kitchen's family.

In a statement via her lawyers, Irwin Mitchell, Linda said her husband's death has been "absolutely devastating" for herself, the couple's two children and four grandchildren.

"Losing Geoff was a crushing blow to the whole family as we all thought he would be around to see his grandchildren grow up," she said.

Singapore Airlines have been approached for comment.
